messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired — PD#4321 — symptom: edge TLS handshakes failing (SNI/TLS 1.3) in eu-west-1. Spike: ~120 TLS errors/min. Link: https://pagerduty.inc/PD4321

pagerduty: PD#4321 auto-escalation to on-call group. Priority: P1. Incident created.

Alex (oncall): ack — I'm on it. pulling logs now. @Priya can you hop on if I need kernel-level traces?

Priya (SRE): ack. grabbing ELB metrics + instance health. tagging this 'edge-tls-eu' for runbook.

Matt: seeing increased 525-level TLS errors on the edge proxies in eu-west-1 from must-gw-proxy nodes. sample log: 
```
2026-03-15T10:12:03Z must-gw-proxy-12 tls: handshake failed: alert: 'unsupported_certificate' remote_ip=3.120.45.22
2026-03-15T10:12:04Z must-gw-proxy-03 tls: handshake failed: alert: 'bad_certificate' remote_ip=3.120.46.11
```

Sara (netops): dig + curl checks: 
```
$ dig +short edge.redwood.example @8.8.8.8
52.48.12.9
\n$ curl -v https://edge.redwood.example --resolve edge.redwood.example:443:52.48.12.9
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS alert, server hello failed: certificate verify failed
```

Lia (support): Support reports multiple customer 5xx rates spiking for inference requests routed to eu-west-1. Major customers: alpha-co (error rate ~40%), beta-inc (calls timeout). Flagging possible customer-impact.

Alex (oncall): initial hypothesis: cert chain mismatch or SNI routing regression after last edge rotation. Priya, can you confirm if cert rotations completed in eu-west earlier?

Priya (SRE): checking cert-rotations service logs... 
```
$ cat /var/log/cert-rotation/2026-03-15.log | grep eu-west-1
2026-03-15T09:58:07 eu-west-1 rotation job started
2026-03-15T09:59:12 eu-west-1 rotation job completed, new cert id=cert-2026-03-15-9
```

Priya (SRE): rotation claimed success but I'm seeing OID mismatch in the chain served by the proxies vs what ACM expects. digging into nginx config on proxies.

Matt: quick mitigation idea — shift traffic off eu-west-1 to eu-central temporarily. We can adjust LB weights to 10% for eu-west and ramp others. That should reduce customer impact while we fix cert chain.

Alex (oncall): go for it. Use canary weight shift, not full cutover. Lia, tell support to inform alpha-co and beta-inc we're mitigating and to expect improvement in ~5-10m.

Priya (SRE): running weight change now: 
```
# traffic-shift (internal tool)
traffic-shift --from-region eu-west-1 --to eu-central-1 --fraction 0.8 --reason "mitigate edge TLS errors"
```

incident-bot: action: traffic-shift job started: job-id ts-5601234567-1. Progress: 0%

Matt: also disabling the recent cert on a small subset of proxies to force fallback to previous cert version while we confirm chain. Command: 
```
sudo mv /etc/ssl/certs/current.pem /etc/ssl/certs/current.pem.bak && sudo cp /etc/ssl/certs/prev.pem /etc/ssl/certs/current.pem && sudo systemctl reload proxy
```

Priya (SRE): done on must-gw-proxy-03 and -12 (2 nodes). Monitoring handshake success.

incident-bot: traffic-shift job update: 50% of traffic moved off eu-west-1.

Sara (netops): after partial revert to prev cert on those nodes, handshake errors dropped from 120/min to ~30/min on those hosts. Overall region error rate down 60%.

Lia (support): support: alpha-co reporting reduced errors. beta-inc still seeing some timeouts for long requests. keeping them posted.

Priya (SRE): root cause narrowed: rotation produced cert with an unexpected intermediate ordering that some edge proxies' TLS stack rejects (library quirk + config). We need to reissue or reorder chain and redeploy correctly. Opening CR for reissue: CR-2026-177.

Alex (oncall): plan: 1) complete rollback of bad cert on all healthy proxies in eu-west (now 30% left) 2) reissue cert with corrected chain 3) staged deploy across region with canary 4) verify metrics and close. Timeline target: complete within 60 minutes.

Matt: executing rollback across managed pool now. Using orchestrator: 
```
orchestrator run --pool eu-west-proxies --action revert-cert --batch-size 10%
```

incident-bot: orchestrator job started: revert-cert job-id rc-5601234567-2. ETA ~25m. PagerDuty: holding auto-escalation.

Priya (SRE): security/infra — please validate the reissued cert chain before redeploy. I'll run `openssl s_client -connect` checks as part of the pipeline.

Lia (support): customer comms updated: "We're aware of TLS handshake failures for requests routed to eu-west-1 and are actively mitigating by shifting traffic and rolling back a recent cert rotation. We'll update within 15 minutes."

incident-bot: revert-cert job update: 100% complete. eu-west proxies now serving previous cert chain. Global TLS errors back to baseline.

Alex (oncall): verifying metrics... good. latency/5xx back to normal across most customers. Lia please run one more customer sanity check and mark alpha-co as recovered if they confirm.

Lia (support): alpha-co and beta-inc confirm recovery. alpha-co sees normal success rates; beta-inc still has a couple of long tail timeouts but much improved.

Priya (SRE): creating follow-up ticket: ENG-2026-889 — investigate cert rotation pipeline to ensure chain ordering preserved. Assign to cert-team + netops. Adding runbook updates: note to validate chain order post-rotation.

Alex (oncall): marking incident as mitigated. Leaving PD alert open until postmortem created. Thanks all.

incident-bot: PD#4321 status: mitigated. Closing automated page. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty: Incident status set to MITIGATED by Alex (oncall). Escalation stopped.

Priya (SRE): Postmortem owners: Priya, Matt. Timeline + commands used will be added to ENG-2026-889. Recommend rotating test certs through staging to catch chain-order regressions.

Matt: quick note for the postmortem: consider adding an automated `openssl verify -CAfile` step in the rotation pipeline. It would have caught the ordering discrepancy.

Alex (oncall): thanks team. I'll file the incident summary and include customer impact metrics. Closing thread in ~1h after postmortem stub created.

incident-bot: Note: runbook link for edge TLS incidents: https://runbook.redwood/edge-tls. Add tags: tls, lb, dns, pagerduty, mitigation
